newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 9.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
CONGRESS TO ELECT NEW PARTY CHIEF TODAY

Congress party delegates are going to the polls to choose their president for the first time in 20 years. This marks a transition in the party's approach to settle the leadership question from consensus method to secret ballot. About 8,000 Pradesh Congress Committee delegates will cast their votes in the nation-wide polls, which come at the end of a no-holds-barred campaign never before witnessed in the party. The secret ballot became inevitable after efforts to arrive at a consensus failed and Sonia Gandhi declined to assume the leadership.
The Times Of India
BIHAR DISSIDENTS WILL ASK LALOO TO PROVE MAJORITY

Dissident leaders of the Janata Dal party (JD) have decided to organise a "self-respect journey" after the election of the new party president. Four ministers dismissed by party chief and Bihar chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav said they will call for a meeting of the JD legislature party under a central observer to ask the chief minister to prove his majority. They accused the chief minister of being authoritarian and running the party organisation as a family business.
The Economic Times
MITSUBISHI SEEKS PARTNER TO ENTER ELEVATOR MARKET

Mitsubishi of Japan is scouting for an Indian partner to tap into the 4.5 billion rupee Indian elevator market. ETA-Melco, a 50:50 joint venture between the Dubai-based ETA and Mitsubishi Electric Company, has recently set up a liaison office in Bangalore. The company made a quiet entry into the Indian market recently. ETA-Melco is keen on having an Indian partner for its venture. Six Mitsubishi officials recently visited India to explore possible partners. Sources said the officials met their counterparts in Kone Elevators India and Johnson, another small, Bangalore-based elevator company.
IDBI FOR FREEZE ON IMPORT DUTIES ON STEEL PRODUCTS

The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) has called for a freeze on import duties on steel products and more protection for the domestic iron and steel industry. The IDBI said that since large investments have already been committed for the creation of additional capacities in the hot rolled and cold rolled coils sectors, it would be desirable to afford some protection to the industry until it gains a competitive advantage. International prices of hot rolled coils have been below $300 a tonne, cutting into the net profits of the top two steel producers in India.
TELECOM MNCS MAY PUT EQUITY VIA 100 PCT SUBSIDIARIES

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) has decided to allow foreign telecom companies to route equity in joint ventures through their wholly owned subsidiaries. The board has allowed U.S.-based Airtouch International to sell its 39 percent equity of RPG Cellcom in favour of its Mauritius-based subsidiary despite objections by the Department of Telecommunications. However the FIPB observed that the routing of equity through a 100 percent subsidiary of the original company should be distinguished from the substitution of a technology partner.
Financial Express
STATE BANK OF INDIA IN TALKS WITH BANKS ABROAD

The State Bank of India (SBI) has initiated talks with a few foreign banks to scrutinise all infrastructure loans. The SBI chairman said the bank is in the process of appraising over 30 infrastructure project proposals worth more than 500 billion rupees. The bank's share in financing these projects will be at least 50 billion to 80 billion rupees. The SBI chief expects slackening commercial credit growth in 1997/98 to be offset by infrastructure lending. He expects a 14-15 percent growth in credit as well as deposits in the current fiscal. The SBI recorded a 13.1 percent growth in deposits and a mere 8.6 percent in credit in the last fiscal year.
The Asian Age
INDIAN TEAM TO LURE US INVESTMENT IN CORE SECTOR

A high-level delegation left for New York to tap foreign investments of up to $15 billion for infrastructural development. The government would like to clear all procedural hurdles in the way of attracting foreign investment, but on India's terms and conditions. Realising that inadequate infrastructure is going to be a key bottleneck threatening future economic growth, the government plans to act swiftly by adopting a fast track approach to attract massive foreign investments in the power, telecommunications, ports, roads, transport, mining and petroleum sectors.
Financial Express
LIC FIRMS UP OVERSEAS EXPANSION PLANS

The Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) has firmed up ambitious plans to expand its international operations in South Asia, Africa and the Gulf. The corporation has decided to completely revamp its existing marginal international operations in Britain and Fiji. It has also decided to set up a new foreign operations department. The chief executive of the department said the presence of 17 million non-resident Indians all over the world provided a major business opportunity for LIC. He said the LIC is targeting markets in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, South Africa, Tanzania and the Gulf, including the UAE.
Business Standard
INFLATION RATE REMAINS AT 6 PCT

The annual rate of inflation based on the wholesale price index (WPI) remained the same at the previous week's level of six percent for the week ended May 17. The annual inflation rate, calculated on a point to point basis, has been declining since February this year, shedding two percentage points since then. The official WPI for all commodities (base 1981/82=100) moved up marginally by 0.1 point during the week under review to 323.5 (provisional) from 323.3 (provisional) the week before. The rate of inflation during the corresponding week of 1996 was 4.45 percent.
BHARAT PETRO TO PICK UP 26 PCT IN CRACKER PROJECT

Bharat Petroleum Corp (BPCL) will hold a 26 percent equity stake in a new joint venture to implement the proposed 65 billion naphtha cracker project in Tamil Nadu. The company will offer another 26 percent to a local or foreign partner through an open tender, while the remaining equity is proposed to be held by financial institutions and the public. The cracker is slated to produce over 500,000 tonnes of ethylene, apart from several down stream products like polypropylene, polyethylene, styrene and butadiene. BPCL sources said they will shortly begin talks with leading domestic and global petrochemicals companies to rope them in for the project.
C.R. BHANSALI OF CRB GROUP ARRESTED

Chain Roop Bhansali, the main accused in the 12 billion rupee finance case that has engulfed his CRB group, was arrested by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) after arriving from Hong Kong. The two were whisked away to the CBI headquarters for interrogation. The CRB group faces liquidation proceedings, and stands accused of irregularities in financial services.
GUJRAL'S OPEN SKIES STANCE JOLTS AIRLINES OFFICIALS

Indian Airlines and Air-India were taken aback by Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's statement about an open skies policy, and they fear an erosion of the bargaining powers of the state-owned carriers during future air traffic negotiations. Speaking in Kathmandu, Gujral said he was dissatisfied with India's civil aviation policy. Officials of the two carriers fear foreign airlines might prefer to wait and see which way the policy was heading rather than conclude bilateral air deals immediately. Gujral's statement was also being widely seen as a green signal to the Tata-Singapore Airlines venture.
FOREIGN PROMOTERS OF POWER PROJECT CONCERND AT DELAY

The foreign promoters of the 1,082 megawatt coal-based Bhadrawati power project have expressed concern over the delay in clearance of the project's power purchase agreement. A letter from the consortium, comprising India's Ispat group, Britain's GEC and France's EDF said the overseas investors and bankers who have been standing behind the project are very concerned about the unexpected developments and the resultant delay. The letter follows a decision by a high-powered central committee to turn down certain tariff allowances recommended by the Maharashtra State Electricity Board and the Maharashtra government.
The Observer
TIME-FRAME TO PHASE OUT IMPORT CURBS MAY BE ALTERED

India will alter its timeframe to phase out quantitative restrictions on imports from nine years to five years if there is pressure from the developed countries. India has already obtained the support of Germany and the United Kingdom for the five-year phase-out plan. The Commerce Ministry had earlier proposed to phase out quantitative restrictions on imports in nine years. But the World Trade Organisation, the United States and European Union have been pressing India to open up its markets, particularly the consumer goods market.
825 MORE ITEMS TO FALL UNDER DUTY ENTITLEMENT SCHEME

The government will announce entitlement rates under the Duty Entitlement Pass Book (DEPB) scheme for 825 more export products by the end of this month. The entitlement rates for 875 export items so far cover sectors like chemicals and wool. The customs department announced entitlement rates of 251 more export products under the DEPB scheme.
EXPORT PROMOTION COUNCIL FOR STEEL PROPOSED

The Ministry of Steel and Mines proposes to constitute an export promotion council to evaluate the potential in different international markets for various steel products. The council will draw strategies from time to time, based on in-house market analysis, to achieve a yearly export target of 15-20 percent of the total production. The proposal has already been submitted to the cabinet for approval. Opening of a stockyard in one of the South East Asian countries is also under consideration. The stockyard, preferably in Thailand, will serve as the gateway to the developing South East Asian countries.
WORST CORPORATE PERFORMANCE IN 10 YEARS

The Centre for Monitoring the Indian Economy (CMIE) has said that corporate results for 1996/97 (April-March) indicated a sharp all-round decline. The performance was the worst recorded by the corporate sector in the last 10 years. Preliminary results from more than 700 companies for 1996/97 were available. The corporate sector has been recording a nearly 20 percent growth a year in nominal sales between 1987/88 and 1995/96. In 1994/95 and 1995/96 the growth rate averaged 25 percent a year. The accelerating pace of sales expansion was severed to half as the sales growth in 1996/97 was barely 11 percent.
